verdict.rationale: Anytype documents a local-first, on-device encrypted Vault, an offline-first app that works without internet, and a local-only mode. Community users confirm it works offline. However, hands-on reports say the on-disk store is opaque Electron blob files that cannot be read or backed up outside the app. Readable data is only available through Anytype's own Markdown export. missing for 10: natively readable on-disk files (plain Markdown/CSV) usable without the app, configurable local storage path.

support.subject: As a power-user, my notes live in local files or a local-first store that I own and can read without the app, and everything keeps working fully offline

citations.quote: A Vault is an encrypted container in Anytype that you own. Everything you create lives inside your Vault, stored directly on your device.
This means an offline-first experience: the app always works without an internet connection
If you prefer to fully keep your data on your device without any server to sync between your desktop and mobile, you can enable local-only mode.
Choose your preferred format: Markdown or Any-Block.
It syncs notes between devices, works offline, is cross-platform
